candidates.title: Anti-AI fonts as future shelf-tag defense
candidates.shift: A typography company has built fonts that show one message to humans and a different one to AI vision systems, to block scraping.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could migrate into retail signage/price tags to blind competitor AI price-scrapers or computer-vision shelf-audits — a strange new front in in-store computer vision. Off-map stretch into TECH/computer-vision branch.
candidates.evidence: Decoy Font uses an optical illusion so chatbots misread text scraped from images; built by Mixfont.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of physical/visual media being redesigned specifically to resist machine perception rather than human perception; if it spreads, retail signage and pricing displays could bifurcate into human-readable and AI-blind layers.
candidates.author: Rima Sabina Aouf

candidates.title: Antarctica as extreme-climate facilities testbed
candidates.shift: Remote, seasonal research stations are adopting digital twins for logistics, open science and station management under extreme isolation.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: extreme-environment facility management (zero-supply-chain-slack, harsh climate, digital twin ops) could become a proving ground for resilient store/DC design in disaster-prone or off-grid retail markets.
candidates.evidence: Paper on integrated digital-twin approaches to Antarctic research station outreach, open science, and management amid remoteness and seasonality.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of extreme-periphery infrastructure management practices (digital twins for near-autonomous remote facilities) potentially diffusing toward disaster-resilient or off-grid commercial real estate design.
candidates.author: Javier Menéndez‐Blázquez

candidates.title: Automated material passports for buildings
candidates.shift: A new spatial-semantic modeling framework automates inventorying of building products, addressing the absence of scalable material-tracking systems needed for circularity compliance.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: fills a real absence — retailers/landlords currently have no automated way to inventory what's actually in their buildings, blocking circular-economy reporting and material reuse markets.
candidates.evidence: ETH Zürich research collection paper on hybrid spatial-semantic modeling for automated building product inventory.
candidates.initial_analysis: Moves construction from undocumented material flows toward machine-readable 'material passports,' a precondition for circular-economy mandates now emerging in EU building codes.
candidates.author: Shuting Mi, Xiaofei Wu, Shunchang Liu et al.

candidates.title: Certifying parts printed by autonomous 3D printers
candidates.shift: A new in-situ, model-based framework proposes non-destructive qualification of parts made by autonomous additive manufacturing, replacing slow post-build inspection.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an absence being filled — construction using autonomous 3D printing currently lacks a fast, trusted certification pathway, which is the real bottleneck to scaling printed structures, not the printers themselves.
candidates.evidence: Journal of Physics Materials paper proposing model-based in-situ qualification and certification for autonomous additive manufacturing parts.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from post-hoc inspection to real-time in-process certification for autonomous manufacturing; if adopted for construction 3D printing, it removes a key regulatory barrier to autonomous on-site building.
candidates.author: Dayalan Gunasegaram, T. DebRoy, Paul Greenway et al.

candidates.title: Algorithmic cannibalization models now vetoing store sites
candidates.shift: A commercial broker reports a retail site rejected specifically because a chain's internal sales-impact model predicted it would cannibalize existing nearby stores.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative single instance: formalized cannibalization algorithms may be quietly hardening into a gatekeeping layer over site selection, shifting real-estate decision power from local judgment to centralized models.
candidates.evidence: Reddit r/CommercialRealEstate poster describes a proposed site rejected per Taco Bell's sales-impact model on surrounding stores.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of algorithmic underwriting displacing human judgment in site selection; if widespread, it standardizes rejection criteria across chains and could freeze out marginal infill locations regardless of local context.

candidates.title: Cool roofs as community-demanded heat infrastructure, South Africa
candidates.shift: A pilot study captures peri-urban South African residents' perceptions of cool-roof passive cooling retrofits amid rising heat.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: bottom-up demand for low-cost passive cooling in the Global South could set a design/material standard (reflective roofing) that wealthier markets later adopt for heat-adaptive retail retrofits.
candidates.evidence: Frontiers in Climate pilot study on community perspectives toward cool-roof intervention in Umlazi, KwaZulu-Natal.
candidates.initial_analysis: Periphery-led heat adaptation at building-envelope scale; if scaled, cool-roof retrofits could become baseline expectation for retail/warehouse roofs in hot climates well before codes require it.
candidates.author: Saloshni Naidoo, Patrick Nyamaruze, Nisha Nadesan-Reddy et al.

candidates.title: Jordan modeling construction-sector circularity readiness
candidates.shift: Expert-evidence structural modeling assesses Jordan's construction sector readiness for circular economy practices around demolition waste.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a peripheral MENA market building its own circularity metrics rather than importing EU frameworks — worth watching whether it becomes a regional standard for Gulf-adjacent construction waste policy.
candidates.evidence: Frontiers in Environmental Economics study using expert evidence and structural modeling on circular economy readiness in Jordan's construction sector.
candidates.initial_analysis: Peripheral-geography case of a resource-constrained construction economy building indigenous circularity metrics; could inform how insurers/financiers price C&D waste risk in similarly water/resource-scarce regions.
candidates.author: Ibrahim Moh’d Saraireh, Faten Albtoush, Mohammed A.KA. Al-Btoush

candidates.title: Concrete waste circularity still missing stakeholder infrastructure
candidates.shift: A conceptual framework maps barriers and strategies for stakeholder collaboration on concrete-waste circularity, the largest share of global C&D waste.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: names the absence directly — no shared governance model exists yet for concrete-waste reuse chains; whoever builds the first working stakeholder protocol could set a de facto industry standard.
candidates.evidence: Journal of Material Cycles and Waste Management conceptual framework on stakeholder engagement barriers for concrete waste circularity.
candidates.source: Journal of Material Cycles and Waste Management
candidates.initial_analysis: Highlights a governance gap rather than a technology gap in construction circularity — the missing piece is coordination infrastructure between demolishers, haulers, recyclers and builders, not new materials science.
candidates.author: Margaret Damilola Oyewole, Daniel W.M. Chan, Donald C. Nwonu et al.

candidates.title: Prefab retrofit supply market maturing in Southern Europe
candidates.shift: A technology supply mapping taxonomizes off-site prefabrication solutions (single-function envelopes etc.) for energy-saving building renovation across Southern Europe.
candidates.ai_read: Trend: prefab retrofit is an already-recognized EU decarbonization strategy — included for context/calibration; the taxonomy itself (function-specific envelope kits) may be the more novel bit for sourcing decisions.
candidates.evidence: Buildings journal systematic mapping of prefabricated retrofit technologies against constructability and circularity constraints in Southern European cases.
candidates.initial_analysis: Standard EU retrofit-acceleration trend; the taxonomy of prefab envelope products could shape how retailers source retrofit kits for aging store stock at scale.
candidates.author: Giulia De Aloysio, S Bassi, Eleonora Sangiorgi et al.

candidates.title: Cold-climate airtightness data from southern Chile
candidates.shift: An experimental study measures airtightness and heating demand in new single-family dwellings built under current code in Temuco, Chile.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: concrete Southern Hemisphere/Latin American benchmark data on whether current codes actually deliver airtightness performance — useful evidence for retailers/developers building in similar cold-temperate peripheral markets.
candidates.evidence: Case Studies in Thermal Engineering experimental study on airtightness and heating demand in new residential buildings in cold-climate Temuco, Chile.
candidates.initial_analysis: Empirical check on whether current regulatory airtightness standards actually hold up in practice in a cold, peripheral Latin American market — a data point for code-enforcement gaps elsewhere.
candidates.author: Carlos Rojas-Herrera, Matías Inostroza, Aner Martínez-Soto et al.

candidates.title: Fire-hardening houses with shingle 'armor'
candidates.shift: Architects renovated their own California mountain house wrapping it in asphalt shingles specifically as wildfire protection.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative single instance: could point to an emerging materials category — cheap, code-friendly fire-cladding retrofits for existing structures — relevant to any retailer or landlord with assets in wildfire-urban-interface zones.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen report on SPF Architects' Mountain Residence renovation using asphalt shingle wrapping for wildfire protection in the Santa Monica Mountains.
candidates.initial_analysis: A single architect-led experiment in retrofit fire-hardening; if it becomes a recognized product category, insurers could start requiring or discounting for such cladding on assets in fire-risk zones.
candidates.author: Jenna McKnight

candidates.title: Securitizing city sensor data to fund infrastructure
candidates.shift: A proposal explores whether data markets and securitization of urban sensor/data streams could close the financing gap for smart-city infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence: no established financial instrument currently exists to turn a building's or city's live sensor data stream into a bankable asset — this paper is an early attempt to define one.
candidates.evidence: Frontiers in Built Environment paper on smart cities, data markets and securitization as financing mechanisms for climate-resilient urban infrastructure.
candidates.initial_analysis: Would create a new asset class where building/store sensor data becomes securitizable collateral for infrastructure finance — directly relevant to the open 'compute/data' hunt zone if it moves from proposal to pilot.
candidates.author: Peter Adriaens, Juri Mattila

candidates.title: Schools built for permanent displacement
candidates.shift: Architecture in borderlands, refugee settlements and climate-displacement sites is being designed as a distinct typology supporting education amid forced mobility.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: signals migration/demographic shift is now generating its own built-environment typology rather than being handled with temporary tents — a leading indicator for how climate/conflict migration reshapes commercial and civic real estate elsewhere.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature on architecture supporting learning in conditions of displacement, borderlands, and climate-induced displacement sites.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from ad hoc temporary shelter toward purpose-built permanent institutions for displaced populations, driven by protracted climate and conflict migration; if it generalizes, retail/civic planners in receiving regions will need new demographic models.
candidates.author: Miwa Negoro

candidates.title: Auction house takes over a modernist icon
candidates.shift: Sotheby's is relocating its global HQ into the restored Marcel Breuer building in New York, adaptively reusing a landmark modernist structure.
candidates.ai_read: Trend: adaptive reuse of iconic underused buildings for prestige corporate HQ is an established pattern — included for context; worth watching whether it foreshadows more department-store-scale reuse of vacant flagship real estate.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily coverage of Herzog & de Meuron + PBDW Architects' restoration of the Breuer building as Sotheby's global headquarters.
candidates.initial_analysis: Confirms continued appetite for reusing iconic mid-century commercial buildings for high-value tenants; a template that could extend to vacant department-store flagships seeking prestige repositioning rather than demolition.
candidates.author: Andreas Luco
